source.title: Therefore I am. I Think
source.authors: Esakkivel Esakkiraja; S. Rajeswar; D. Akhiyarov; Rajagopal Venkatesaramani

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Conceptually tests early-encoded decisions and their causal influence using probes and activation steering, but studies tool-use decisions rather than future-token representations in verse.
record.gate_note: The paper cites rhyme-planning and future-token-decoding results from other work; those cited results are not this study's findings. It measures pre-generation tool-decision probes, steering effects on actions and reasoning length, and judge-classified behavior. Judge bucket distributions are not separately rowed here because they describe the qualitative response to the intervention rather than a distinct measure of whether an early feature causally shapes subsequent text; their findings are summarized in authors_conclusion and problems.
record.test_reason: The study decodes a later action (tool call or not, made after the whole reasoning trace) from activations before any reasoning token. Steering that pre-generation direction changes the later action and the chain of thought. This is internal look-ahead in a new task, tool-use reasoning, so it bears on V5. It does not test V3's question of why the feature is computed (for later use versus as a next-token side effect), and it does not involve verse or token-identity prediction.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that tool-call decisions are linearly decodable from pre-generation activations and that steering that direction causally flips actions in 7–79% of cases, depending on model and benchmark. When actions flip, the CoT often rationalizes the flip, which they argue undermines CoT faithfulness. Some examples resist steering while their reasoning inflates.
record.recipe_differences: Uses logistic-regression probes on residual-stream activations and mean-difference activation steering for tool/no-tool decisions in reasoning models; it does not use rhyme-word attribution graphs or rhyme-specific interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering outcomes vary with model, benchmark, intervention direction, steering strength, and thinking versus no-think mode. GLM-Z1-9B no-think mode is unavailable; GLM on BFCL uses alpha values 10, 20, and 30 because of larger activation norms.

fits_no_version.finding: Under steering, the chain of thought often rationalizes the induced action (confabulated support, constraint override) rather than resisting it. Judge-classified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning-model chain of thought post-hoc rationalizes internally pre-encoded action decisions.

record.problems: Steering evaluations use 100 held-out examples per direction and provide no uncertainty intervals for the reported flip rates. Exact probe AUROC values are shown only in figures and are not stated in the text. Qualitative rationalization judgments rely on two LLM judges; their agreement varies by setting, with reported disagreement rates from 7.0% to 38.0%. The experiments concern tool-use actions, not future-token or rhyme representations, and do not rule out the possibility that early signals arise as a side effect of next-token prediction.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 CoT token-inflation results and Tables 3–5 behavioral-judge bucket distributions were not entered as separate rows. They concern reasoning-length changes or qualitative categories under steering, rather than additional measurements of the version's central early-feature/action effect.

untested.parts: No verse, no rhyme words, no frontier model.
No prediction of token identities several positions ahead; the probe target is a binary action.
Does not test whether the pre_gen feature exists for later positions rather than as a next-token side effect.
No rhyme planning in open models.
Chess and Sokoban are not tested. Only tool-use decisions in two reasoning models, plus GPT-OSS-20B probes only.
No test of plan horizon or of local-heuristic explanations.

missing.what: Pre_gen probe decisions agree with think_end probe decisions over 80% of the time; probe AUROC dips early in reasoning and then recovers.
CoT token inflation under steering, e.g. Qwen When2Call suppression flips 1.38x and resisted cases 2.30x.
GPT-OSS-20B shows strong pre_gen predictability but lower early agreement with think_end (probes only, no steering).

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked everything to V3. V3 asks whether features are computed for the benefit of later positions, which this study does not separate from side effects; V5 (look-ahead in other tasks) is the better fit, so rows were relinked. Fixed the dangling id: the labels cited q-w-s-t4, but the row is q-w-s-t. Flip rates have n=100 per direction and no confidence intervals. The only flip baseline is the 0% unrelated-direction control. Relatively strong steering (alpha up to 30) raises off-manifold concerns.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming verse, candidate rhyme words, or intervention on rhyme-word representations.
No prediction of tokens several positions ahead from a hidden state; the probe predicts a tool/no-tool action.
Tests early encoding and causal steering of tool-use decisions, not whether the feature is computed specifically for later positions rather than as a side effect of next-token prediction.
No rhyme-planning test in open-weight models using attribution graphs or rhyme-specific probing.
Tests tool-use decisions, not multi-step reasoning, chess, or Sokoban look-ahead.
Does not test how far ahead a plan reaches or whether the signal is a local next-token feature or heuristic.

relationships.condition: Tool-use decisions in Qwen3-4B and GLM-Z1-9B, pre_gen probe and higher-strength steering
relationships.reason: Pre_gen AUROC exceeds 90% in all four cases (probe-1). Steering flips actions in both directions, up to 49–79% (q-w-s-t12, q-w-i-t12, q-b-i-t12, g-b-s-30, g-b-i-30), while the unrelated-direction control flips 0% (ctrl-1).
relationships.display_finding: Pre-generation probes exceeded 90% AUROC in all four cases, and stronger steering changed actions in both directions at rates reaching 49–79%, versus 0% for an unrelated-direction control.

relationships.condition: Low steering strength, no-think mode, and GLM on When2Call
relationships.reason: Flips are often small: 2–16% at alpha 4 (q-w-s-nt4, g-w-i-4). GLM When2Call suppression stays at 9–11% at every alpha (g-w-s-4, g-w-s-8, g-w-s-12). No-think is consistently less steerable than thinking (q-w-s-nt12 vs q-w-s-t12). Many examples resist steering.
relationships.display_finding: Action flips were often only 2–16% at alpha 4, GLM When2Call suppression stayed at 9–11% across strengths, no-think mode was consistently less steerable than thinking, and many examples resisted intervention.

tranche.reason: Tests internal look-ahead in the new setting of tool-use action selection, with pre-reasoning probes and activation steering.

source_check.notes: The pre_gen-derived steering vector is applied during both prefill and decoding, so the intervention does not isolate causality at the pre-generation position alone. The abstract's 7–79% range omits lower Table 1 rates, including 2%.

reader_labels.condition: Pre-generation action probes and steering across the tested models and benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: Pre-generation probes predict action decisions at over 90% in all four main model-benchmark cases, and steering changes action outcomes in both directions; see probe-1 and the steering rows.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Held-out steering tests across models, benchmarks, strengths, and modes
reader_labels.reason: Flip rates are incomplete and vary substantially with model, benchmark, direction, mode, and strength; some are low, and the paper notes resistant examples. The study also does not distinguish purpose-built future features from next-token side effects.
